title: regional-gpu-burst-and-kv-warmup-scenarios-q2-2026
content:
Executive summary:

This worksheet models the region-by-region GPU and KV-cache impact for onboarding Model-X (xxL open-architecture variant) across our hosted and dedicated fleets. The goal is to give SRE/infra and product teams a small set of scenarios to pick an initial rollout cadence that keeps latency SLOs and avoids >85% sustained GPU utilization in any region, while bounding additional KV footprint.

Highlights (short):
- Baseline global qps estimate for feature = 2.7k qps (weighted by usage from product analytics).
- Expected peak multiplier during initial marketing + pilot: 3.2x baseline (burst window 1h/day typical).
- KV warm-up (per-request KV inflation) expected to increase per-session KV bytes by ~18–40% during first 48 hours after model becomes available in a region depending on client behavior.
- Primary mitigations: staged rollout (region-by-region, % traffic ramp), pre-warm flows for known high-QPS customers, conservative autoscale thresholds with faster spin-up on dedicated pools.

Key assumptions and sources:
- Model-X nominal token cost: 1.1 tokens/sec per user-request average compute profile (this is a simplified abstraction for planning).
- Average generated tokens per request: 120 tokens.
- Average request size (input tokens): 40 tokens.
- Effective tokens-per-request = 160 tokens.
- GPUs: A single rtx-A100-equivalent (our unit) can sustain ~1,100 effective tokens/sec under current kernel set for mixed-precision quantized variant at 512 context. For longer contexts cost grows ~1.9x at 2048 ctx.
- Typical per-GPU sustained throughput target for safe headroom: 70% of peak (so planning capacity ~= 770 tokens/sec per GPU).
- Baseline KV cache: current steady-state global KV footprint for similar models is 42 TB; Model-X expected cold-warm incremental KV footprint estimate: 0.9–1.8 TB per major region depending on session length distribution.
- Cache hit improvement from prefix caching expected after warmup: +10–22% reduction in compute tokens for warmed users.

Scenarios modeled:
1) Conservative staged rollout (recommended): 10% traffic to region for first 24h, 25% for next 48h, full after 7 days. Autoscale min nodes pre-allocated = baseline GPUs + 10% buffer.
2) Aggressive (rapid 100% rollout): immediate availability for all users; assume 3.2x burst on day 0. Requires large pre-warm or significant autoscale events.
3) Customer-first (pre-warm customers only): limit initial availability to enterprise/canary customers with pre-warm SDKs and reserved capacity, surface to product as "early access".

Per-region micro-simulations (representative output, numbers rounded):

Table: region | baseline qps | peak burst qps (3.2x) | effective tokens/sec at peak | GPUs needed (70% headroom) | KV warmup GB (48h window)
us-west | 820 | 2,624 | 2,624 * 160 tokens / sec-profile = 419,840 tokens/sec equivalent | 545 GPUs -> planned 600 GPUs total | 1,150 GB
us-east | 910 | 2,912 | 466,000 tokens/sec equivalent | 605 GPUs -> planned 660 GPUs total | 1,320 GB
eu-west | 560 | 1,792 | 286,720 tokens/sec equivalent | 373 GPUs -> planned 410 GPUs total | 960 GB
apac-sg | 260 | 832 | 133,120 tokens/sec equivalent | 173 GPUs -> planned 190 GPUs total | 720 GB
eu-central | 180 | 576 | 92,160 tokens/sec equivalent | 120 GPUs -> planned 140 GPUs total | 540 GB

Notes on table calculations:
- The 'effective tokens/sec at peak' is estimated as peak_qps * average_tokens_per_request / average_latency_window (we simplified to aggregate token rate for capacity). For operational planning we convert to required GPUs by dividing by 770 tokens/sec (70% safe target).
- GPUs needed values are intentionally conservative (rounded up) and include an additional 10% buffer for warmup churn.

KV footprint modelling details:
- Per-session KV entry size observed for similar models: 8–16 KB per active prefix slot.
- Average concurrent active sessions per 1k qps: 1,200 sessions (because sessions persist and many users stream multiple requests).
- Cold-to-warm growth profile: day0: +40% relative KV insertion churn; day1: +22%; day2: +12%; stabilizes at +6% over baseline by day7. This is due to repeated prompt variations during early trials.
- If we onboard simultaneously in multiple regions without pre-warm, global KV cache insertion rate may exceed provisioned network/writes and lead to cache pressure; recommended policy is write-throttle for first 48h or prioritized writes for enterprise customers.

Operational risk matrix (short):
- Risk: GPU oversubscription during burst. Severity: high. Mitigation: staggered rollout + immediate autoscale (pre-warm spot pool conversion to reserved for 2h).
- Risk: Cache eviction storms causing increased cold misses and higher latencies. Severity: medium-high. Mitigation: increase slot retention window temporarily, enable aggressive prefix consolidation for new model, and observe hit-rate metric every 15 minutes.
- Risk: Regional networking saturations due to KV replication. Severity: medium. Mitigation: limit replication RPS, perform write-batching, throttle client SDKs when writes exceed threshold.

Suggested rollout plan (operational playbook):
1) Week -1: Run internal pre-warm in us-west using synthetic flows that mimic high-variance prompts (ticket: INFRA-4827). Validate KV-insert RPS and eviction curves.
2) Day 0 (canary): enable feature for 5% traffic in us-west + 2 enterprise pre-warm customers. Monitor: per-GPU utilization, 99th p99 latency (generation), KV insertion RPS, cache hit%. Hold for 6 hours.
3) Day 1–2: ramp to 25% in us-west; enable read-only pre-warm in us-east. If p99 < target and HDD writes < threshold, move to Day 3.
4) Day 3–7: region-by-region rollouts with the same cadence; do not exceed two concurrent region ramp-ups unless pre-approved by on-call infra lead.
5) Post 7 days: treat as general availability; reduce write-throttles and return slots to normal retention.

Monitoring and dashboards to create (KPIs):
- Per-region GPU utilization heatmap (1m/5m/1h) with alert at >80% sustained for 5m.
- KV insert RPS and eviction rate with alert when insert RPS > X (region-specific threshold).
- Model-specific p99 generation latency with alert at +30% over baseline.
- Customer-impact scoreboard: list of enterprise customers with pre-warm status and ticket owner.

Immediate action items (owners + due dates):
- Aisha: finalize pre-warm synthetic script and schedule run (due 2026-02-12).
- Liam: add temporary autoscale policy for Model-X (min buffer + fast spin-up) and PR the policy (GH PR: 3148) (due 2026-02-14).
- Sofia: create KV write-throttle mechanism and dashboard (due 2026-02-16).
- Diego: validate regional network replication SLOs with cloud provider (due 2026-02-15).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Should we prefer spinning up dedicated reserved capacity in us-east vs relying on autoscale? (Cost vs latency tradeoff — product to decide).
- Exact spot-to-reserved conversion time target (we currently assume 5m spin-up is possible; need SRE confirmation).
- Simulated user prompt diversity: do we have a bench dataset representing the expected 40% prefix variance? If not, product to provide sample prompt sets.

Appendix (quick calculation examples):
- Example GPU calc (simplified):
  region_peak_tokens_sec = peak_qps * avg_tokens_per_request
  gpus_required = ceil(region_peak_tokens_sec / 770)

- Example KV insertion estimate (48h):
  estimated_new_slots = baseline_concurrent_sessions * (cold_inflation_pct)
  incremental_kv_GB = estimated_new_slots * avg_slot_kb / 1024

Raw simulation notes (for reviewers who want the spreadsheet):
- I ran a short Monte Carlo for 10k trials varying session length (Exp(1/5)), prompt prefix variance (uniform 0.2–0.6), and peak multiplier (2.4–3.8). The conservative 3.2x was chosen to be between median and 75th percentile.
- Simulation workbook saved as INFRA-4827-sim-v2. Sheet tabs: inputs, regional-sims, kv-warmup-curves, autoscale-behavior.

If you are reviewing: please check the per-region baseline qps assumptions (derived from product analytics snapshot 2026-02-05) and call out any enterprise customers that must be pre-warmed.

Document history: draft created 2026-02-10 by Aisha, updates: 2026-02-12 (added simulation runs), 2026-02-14 (autoscale policy PR link), 2026-02-18 (final numbers rounded for planning).
